notes: The database is the auth SQLite file at `AUTH_SQLITE_PATH` (`/data/auth.sqlite` in production), not `$DATA_DIR/app.sqlite`, and keeps that name and location.

Migrations stay in drizzle-auth/ (drizzle.auth.config.ts, scripts `auth:db:generate` and `auth:db:check`) with their full history, and scripts/nodeAuthSqlite.ts applies them through node:sqlite before the server starts, detecting each by the table or column it adds; production has no `__drizzle_migrations` table, so the recipe's migrator would replay 0000 against existing tables.

src/server/localAuthDatabase.ts opens the client with `concurrency: 1` and a 5 s busy timeout, and holds the auth and OAuth provider schemas; backups are the hourly Dokploy schedule from scripts/dokployAuthSchedule.ts, not a pre-migration `VACUUM INTO`.
The recipe's starter schema and migrations, and its tests of the migrator, are left out; sqliteAuth.integration.test.ts and the nodeAuthSqlite tests cover the real database.
`app().auth` is synchronous, because the file is migrated before the Nitro process starts and Better Auth is created with the client directly.

The telemetry instance lives in src/server/serverTelemetry.ts as a `globalSingleton`, not in `app()`, because rpc, request middleware, background jobs, and the push senders report before or outside the composition root; it is created from an empty environment outside production, so local and test runs send nothing.

src/server/telemetry.ts takes a second `options` argument for the application's service version, the `deployment.host` resource attribute, and the `$host`/`app_version` before_send filter, which earlier events and dashboards carry.

src/server/shutdown.ts (a Nitro close hook) shuts down every singleton with a `shutdown`, the server telemetry and the MCP analytics client, with a 2 s deadline that fits the 3 s scripts/nodeServer.ts gives the Nitro process after its own drain.
rpc.ts looks up the signed-in user only on a reporting instance and passes it to `observeServerFunction`; `inTurn` reports streamed per-item failures the same way.
`posthog.capture` is synchronous, so callers no longer await captures; telemetry callbacks in sqliteAuth.ts and photoScreening.ts are typed as returning nothing.
src/server/push.ts and src/server/webPush.ts moved from src/adapters/ because they report through server telemetry, which the layer rules keep adapters from importing.
A server exception without a known person gets posthog-node's random distinct id instead of the shared `server` person the v5 helper used.
`bundledPostHog` is undefined outside a production build, because a local dev server shares the production project token; the ingest proxy then answers 404 in development.

`serviceName` is `praetorium`, and the browser's logs and metrics keep reporting as `praetorium` (with the package version) instead of `praetorium-web`, which existing log views and alerts filter on; the server reports as `praetorium-server` as before.

src/client/posthog.tsx merges `applicationPostHogOptions` from src/posthog.ts over `postHogOptions`: dead clicks, more masked URL parameters (`state`, `code_challenge`, `sig`), before_send filters for impersonation, unactionable exceptions, private URLs and feature context, masked log URLs, and no session recording on the stream overlay, which is decided at init from the page's path.
The router keeps its own `defaultOnCatch` (`reportRouteError`), which captures route exceptions after its module-recovery handling, and every route has the application's `defaultErrorComponent`.
scripts/posthogSourceMaps.ts uploads symbol sets named `praetorium-web` at the commit (`GITHUB_SHA`), which error tracking matches releases by.

Dockerfile.node keeps its own upload: the BuildKit secret is `posthog_api_key` (from the `POSTHOG_API_KEY` Actions secret), it retries the build and a `posthog-cli sourcemap upload` of `.output/public`, and deletes every remaining map.
Vite's `telemetry` chunk group keeps posthog-js and the PostHog packages in their own chunk.

src/server/app.ts is the application's own composition root, a `globalSingleton` (src/lib/globalSingleton.ts) holding the catalogue loaders, SpacetimeDB operator, auth, and background jobs; it has no AsyncDisposableStack or closeApp, because scripts/nodeServer.ts owns process shutdown and the combat worker pool closes from src/server/warmPlugin.ts.
src/lib/globalSingleton.ts keys values by name under one registered symbol, because Nitro plugins are bundled apart from the request bundle and must share the combat worker pool with it.

The root route keeps the document in AppShell as its `component`, since the shell renders two different documents (the stream overlay and the app frame) around its providers; the chunk recovery script is in head() and the update notice in the app frame's body.
The router keeps the application's own context (`origin` for absolute metadata), stale-build reload, route error recovery, view transitions, and error and not-found components.
src/client/queryClient.ts keeps the application's caches, offline snapshot restore, and failure reporting around `new QueryClient`, and its own tests in place of the recipe's.

src/start.ts runs request timing first, then the recipe's middleware, then the crawler log, shared page cache, and public page load limits; function middleware adds the pending-write marker, and `serverFns.fetch` keeps the network error handling.
`referrer-policy` stays `no-referrer`, the application's privacy choice, instead of `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.

src/server/contentSecurityPolicy.ts adds the faction icon CDN and PostHog media hosts to img-src, the rules text host to connect-src, and `worker-src 'self' blob:` for combat workers; src/server/cspPlugin.ts (a Nitro response hook) still widens img-src with the deployment's public asset origin and adds `'unsafe-eval'` when SpacetimeDB is configured, since both are runtime settings.
Static files Nitro serves no longer carry the security headers the Nitro `/**` route rule added; they still get their Cache-Control rules there.
src/server/rpc.ts wraps the recipe's `run` in the application's PostHog observer and reports failures through it; `inTurn` streams per-item results with the same reporting.

/api/health waits for the catalogue warm-up and checks the auth database and SpacetimeDB through `app().health()`, maps failures to `database_unavailable`, and adds `x-praetorium-revision`, which preview and release checks read.
src/server/requestOrigin.ts keeps `siteOrigin`, the isomorphic origin for page metadata, on top of `publicOrigin`.

Forwarded headers count only with `TRUST_PROXY=true`, where the application trusted them always; every deployment, preview, and local stack sets `APP_URL`, which `acceptedOrigins` and `publicOrigin` use instead.
AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md, so the recipe paragraph sits in CLAUDE.md beside the application's own agent guide.

Packages stay at the versions the v5 managed install had locked (vitest 5, oxlint 1.87, oxfmt 0.72, typescript 7.0.2, vite 8.3.4) and exact, so the migration changes no tool behaviour; Dependabot moves them.
packageManager stays pnpm 12.13.0, which the application, its dev container, and CI already use.

`check` keeps the application's extra gates (docs lint, vocabulary, changesets, auth migrations, catalogue pins, Python tests), and `typecheck` also checks the mobile and spacetimedb workspace packages.
`lint` adds `--report-unused-disable-directives-severity=error`, which the application already enforced.
`changesets:check` runs scripts/checkChangesets.ts, the frontmatter and package-name check `ras changesets check` did, because the application releases with Changesets.
tsconfig.json keeps the application's include list, `@/*` path, and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`; e2e/ is type-checked by Playwright's own transform, as before.
.oxlintrc.json also extends the domain preset and keeps the application's core and component layer rules.
vitest.config.ts is the application's: the forks pool, the `@` alias, mobile and spacetimedb tests, and separate unit and integration configs.
pnpm-workspace.yaml is a workspace of the application, mobile/, and spacetimedb/, and keeps its own allowBuilds and packageExtensions.
